explanation: Charles V’s expedition of 1535 was a counter-offensive against Barbarossa’s capture of Tunis the year before, and the 1534 article uses that word. “Conquest of Tunis (1534)”, at revision 1370612766: “Barbarossa thus established a strong naval base in Tunis, which could be used for raids in the region, and on nearby Malta … In 1535 however, upon the plea of Muley Hasan, Emperor Charles V mounted a counter-offensive and retook the city in the conquest of Tunis of 1535.” The second author, “Conquest of Tunis (1535)” at revision 1375228138, § Background, puts the same answer in the verb: “Barbarossa established a strong naval base in Tunis … Charles V was informed that should Barbarossa remain in power in Tunis, both Italy and Spain might be threatened by the Ottoman navy. He therefore assembled a large fleet to drive the Ottomans from the region.” `reacted-to`, running forward in time from the capture to the answer to it. `probable`, on the articles alone (rule 22).
